The group demands excessive and **uncritical commitment** to its ideology or leader. Questioning is discouraged or morally punished. A polarized mentality emerges: the world is divided between the chosen and the enemy. The ends justify the means. Doctrine takes precedence over personal experience and contradictory evidence. The member’s identity is constructed more through opposition to an adversary than through any coherent positive content. Leaders are not truly held accountable: their lies or contradictions are reinterpreted, ignored, or transformed into evidence of their moral superiority.

Added to this is **psychological denial as a defense mechanism.** Accepting facts that contradict the narrative would mean allowing reality to cease being what the believer needs it to be. That is why **evidence fails to penetrate**. **Reason itself becomes an existential threat**. Facts that contradict the narrative—historical failures, human costs, internal inconsistencies, empirical results—are not debated. They are reinterpreted, relativized, or attributed to the enemy. **The believer simply “does not see” the evidence.** He neutralizes it to avoid having to change his identity.

This process explains why **certain groups can maintain contradictory claims without experiencing discomfort, why external criticism reinforces rather than weakens adherence, and why rational dialogue becomes sterile. This is no longer a debate over ideas. It is a defense of a psychological and group identity.**
